Moresheth-gath
MOR-esh-eth-GATH
proper noun
Hebrew Moresheth Gath, “possession of Gath,” a town of the Judean lowland, the home of the prophet Micah, distinct from the Philistine Gath.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

📖 Biblical Definition

Moresheth-gath was Micah’s own home, for he is called “the Morasthite” (Mic 1:1) — the man of Moresheth. In his lament over the doomed towns of the lowland, the prophet does not spare the region of his birth: “Therefore shalt thou give presents to Moreshethgath: the houses of Achzib shall be a lie to the kings of Israel” (Mic 1:14). The image is of a father giving a parting dowry to a daughter passing away to another house — Judah must send Moresheth-gath off like a bride departing, surrendered to the conqueror. Micah, who “saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem” (Mic 1:1), declared that the blow had reached Judah’s gate: “he is come unto the gate of my people, even to Jerusalem” (Mic 1:9), and bade the land mourn its captive children (Mic 1:16). Moresheth-gath preaches that the true prophet spares not even his own. Micah wept for his homeland yet spoke its doom plainly, loving his people too well to flatter them. The faithful watchman does not exempt his own house, his own town, his own kindred, from the word of God. Nathan of the manse and Amos of the herds and Micah of Moresheth all learned that the word entrusted to them must fall where God aims it, even upon the fields where they were born.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The lowland home of the prophet Micah (Mic 1:1,14), distinct from Philistine Gath; a witness that the faithful prophet spares not even his own homeland from the word of God.

MORESHETH-GATH, “possession of Gath,” a town of the Judean lowland.

The home of the prophet Micah, called “the Morasthite” (Mic 1:1).

Distinct from the Philistine city of Gath.

Named in Micah’s lament, surrendered like a departing bride (Mic 1:14).

A witness that the true prophet spares not his own homeland.

📖 Key Scripture

Mic 1:14 — "Therefore shalt thou give presents to Moreshethgath: the houses of Achzib shall be a lie to the kings of Israel."

Mic 1:1 — "The word of the LORD that came to Micah the Morasthite in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem."

Mic 1:9 — "For her wound is incurable; for it is come unto Judah; he is come unto the gate of my people, even to Jerusalem."

Mic 1:16 — "Make thee bald, and poll thee for thy delicate children; enlarge thy baldness as the eagle; for they are gone into captivity from thee."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The prophet Micah’s own homeland, not spared in his lament; the entry recovers that the faithful watchman exempts not even his own from the word of God.

expand to see more

Moresheth-gath rebukes the partiality that would soften God’s word where it touches our own. Micah loved his native lowland, yet he pronounced its doom without flinching, giving it up like a father surrendering a daughter to a far country. He wept, but he did not flatter.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the impartial faithfulness of the true prophet, who spares neither his own town nor his own kindred when God aims the word there. The temptation of every minister is to preach hardest against sins that are far off and to fall silent where the word would wound his own. But Micah of Moresheth, Amos of Tekoa, and Nathan before David all learned that the message belongs to God, not to the messenger’s comfort. Love for one’s people is proved, not by flattery, but by faithfulness that tells them the truth even to their loss.
